did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jonah is not happy that Nineveh was spared; instead, he is deeply distressed and angry because the disaster he had foretold did not happen.

Did you know? Jonah explains that he fled to Tarshish because he knew that the Lord is “gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love,” and might relent from bringing disaster.
Did you know? In his anger, Jonah asks the Lord to take his life and even says, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
Did you know? Jonah leaves Nineveh, settles east of the city, and builds a shelter so he can wait and see what will happen to it.
Did you know? The Lord provides Jonah with a plant that grows up over him and gives him shade. Jonah is very happy about the plant because it eases his discomfort.
Did you know? The next day, the Lord provides a worm that attacks the plant, and it withers. Jonah’s condition changes rapidly as a result.
Did you know? After the plant withers, the sun and the hot east wind make Jonah so miserable that he faints and again asks to die.
Did you know? The Lord compares Jonah’s pity for the plant—which he did not work for or grow—with the Lord’s compassion for Nineveh.

Did you know? The book ends with a question about the Lord’s compassion for great Nineveh, where there are more than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, as well as many animals.
